svg.title: Real-Time Intelligence: Hot Path vs Cold Path Routing
svg.desc: A decision/internals diagram. An Eventstream receives an event and routes it to two paths simultaneously, not exclusively. The hot path sends the event to Activator, which evaluates threshold, pattern, or KQL-defined conditions and fires an action (notification, pipeline, Copy job, Power Automate) within seconds, with no polling schedule. The cold path writes the event into an Eventhouse KQL database, where it becomes durable, queryable, and available to notebooks, Power BI, and Fabric data agents, at the cost of ingestion and indexing latency the hot path does not pay. A warning node covers Eventhouse's three-stage capacity throttling ladder, and a worked example traces one vehicle-offline event through both paths.
svg.text: Real-Time Intelligence — Hot Path vs Cold Path Internals
Microsoft Fabric · Fabric Atlas original diagram · decision & internals view

g.aria-label: Does this event need an immediate reaction?
g.title: Does this event need an immediate reaction? — Routing decision: does the event need to trigger an action now, or be queried later, or both?
g.text: ROUTING DECISION — WHERE DOES AN INCOMING EVENT GO?

g.title: Eventstream ingest & routing — Events arrive from Kafka, MQTT, CDC, or Fabric/OneLake sources and route to one or more destinations.
g.text: An Eventstream operator (filter / dedup / windowed aggregation / routing) evaluates every event and fans out to both paths [claims a7afa4e0, b5ae3ebc]
→ Needs a reaction in seconds, no historical joins? Route to HOT path (Activator / Live Map).

g.title: Eventhouse KQL database (cold path) — Durable, indexed, queryable storage — feeds notebooks, ML, Power BI, and data agents.
g.text: → Needs to be queried later, joined with history, or trained against? Route to COLD path (Eventhouse / KQL DB).
Both are not mutually exclusive: a derived eventstream commonly feeds BOTH paths from the same source event [claim b5ae3ebc].

g.title: Activator (hot path) — Monitors threshold, pattern, or KQL-defined conditions and fires an action within seconds, no polling.
g.text: Fires on Real-Time hub, KQL query, or Power BI report data
No polling schedule — events trigger rules directly [claim 6347cb60]
mirrored to OneLake as Delta-Parquet (no extra copy)
Fabric notebooks run KQL, T-SQL, Python, or Spark
directly over Eventhouse data — no data movement [946493a7]
exploration, transformation & ML share one surface

g.title: OneLake Delta mirror — Adaptive-batched write exposes KQL data as Delta, queryable by Direct Lake, Warehouse, Lakehouse, Spark.
g.text: 3 · OneLake Delta Mirror to BI & Downstream
Delta-Parquet mirror consumed by Power BI Direct Lake mode,
Lakehouse/Warehouse engines, or Real-Time hub catalog entries
Optimized for: reaction latency, live visualization, event-driven orchestration
State: transient in eventstream / condition evaluation — not a query store
Trigger model: fully event-driven, no polling schedule required [claim 6347cb60]
Optimized for: historical query, cross-field joins, model training, audit
State: durable in Eventhouse, queryable via KQL/T-SQL/Python/Spark [946493a7]
Trigger model: pull-based query, or feeds Activator's KQL conditions

g.title: Warning: three-stage capacity throttling — Sustained overload degrades the cold path in three escalating stages, up to data-loss risk.
g.text: Same source event, two destinations: HOT path evaluates KQL Activator condition ("no ping > 3 min") and opens incident within seconds —
COLD path lands pings in Eventhouse so an analyst queries vehicle route history later. Warning: capacity overload triggers 3-stage throttling.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset.
